payload.summary: Planned the agent runtime correctness change after a design review of ACA's agent surfaces against the enterprise memory-platform specification. Gate 1 selected Approach 3 with a defer-until-event queue mechanism: agent tasks become the agent_task.execute operation type, approvals become approval.wait child operations, memory strategies are built from settings on a new async session factory, partial memory writes are reported, and cost flows from one pricing source. Tier is coordinated with six packages, three of them parallel after wp-contracts.

decisions.title: Agent tasks are a canonical operation type
decisions.rationale: execute_agent_task was a legacy string handler with no idempotency, cancel, list, or events; registering agent_task.execute in the v2 registry gives all four and removes the ad-hoc re-enqueue.

decisions.title: Approvals are approval.wait child operations with a decision result
decisions.rationale: Denial is a valid outcome, not a failure; the parent resumes from a checkpoint the way pipeline.run resumes on ingestion children.

decisions.title: Defer-until-event generalizes the existing batch parent reset
decisions.rationale: OperationService.defer re-polls every second; a human approval can take hours. A wait_on marker plus a child-terminal wake inside the same transaction reuses the summarization.run reset path instead of adding a second notification channel.

decisions.title: Async engine confined to memory strategies
decisions.rationale: Vector and keyword strategies require an async session factory that did not exist; asyncpg is already a dependency. The factory is imported only under src/agents/memory and a test asserts that.

decisions.title: Embedding column follows the configured model
decisions.rationale: agent_memories.embedding was vector(1536) while the default local model is 384-dim; the migration interpolates the dimension at migration time, the documented pg_cron pattern.

decisions.title: Tier: coordinated
decisions.rationale: Coordinator reachable with lock, queue, and discover; feature spans queue, agents, storage, and contracts.

next_steps: Start with wp-contracts (tasks 1.1 to 1.3); wp-queue-wait, wp-memory-infra, and wp-cost can run in parallel once it lands.
